classes.description: SpecGraph's verifier that reads the published bundle and compares it with retained local artifacts.
The bundle served at the selected HTTPS base URL for this verification attempt.
The local bundle supplying exact metadata bytes and the manifest of expected payload paths and digests.
Compare the published bundle against the selected retained bundle.
Concrete condition used to validate whether a requirement or specification is satisfied.
Derived executable or source-facing surface that implements specifications.
Rule or boundary that limits valid graph, specification, or implementation behavior.
Chosen design or product direction that constrains later specification and implementation work.
Directed typed relation between two nodes.
Traceable support for acceptance, validation, and review decisions.
A reviewable epistemic claim that may inform interpretation without becoming intent or authorizing promotion.
Governed representation of what the product must be and how it can be validated.
A pre-canonical synthesis of one or more intent fragments and optional context, not an approved Intent.
A partial observable intent signal that does not by itself constitute a complete intent draft.
Condition that must remain true across valid graph evolution.
First-class graph entity with stable identity, lifecycle, provenance, and versioned state.
A reviewable candidate operationalization of intent, distinct from its motivating intent and not itself an approval.
Packaged delivery state that contains derived code surfaces and their validation evidence.
Verifiable product or system obligation that can be checked by acceptance criteria or tests.
Versioned specification artifact that refines intent into machine-readable requirements and decisions.
Executable product ontology that represents intent, specifications, graph structure, and derived code surfaces.
Validation artifact that checks requirements, specifications, or implementation behavior.
A proposed canonical destination and identity, not proof that an artifact exists.
Attempt canonical materialization of a draft against its ingress and a separate decision.

fields.description: Identifies the existing recorded ingress into this draft.
Identifies a selected destination, which need not already exist as a canonical artifact.
Identifies the separate draft-to-canonical transition record.

classes.description: Attempt the proposal-to-draft transition against a separately recorded review.

fields.description: Identifies the selected candidate draft; a reference does not approve it.
Identifies the proposal-to-draft transition record for independent validation.

classes.description: A proposed contextual role for an actor initiating a promotion, without implied authority.
A reviewable pre-canonical draft; a recorded ingress is required before materialization.
A completed decision for one promotion edge; pending templates are outside this class.
A person or agent acting to synthesize fragments into a candidate draft in this interpretation.
Interpret a fragment in the context of an existing candidate intent draft.

fields.description: The candidate draft for which the fragment is interpreted; the application resolves this reference.

classes.description: Interpret an intent in the context of an existing candidate proposal.

fields.description: The candidate for which the intent is interpreted; the application resolves this reference.

classes.description: A person or agent acting as the author of a candidate proposal in this interpretation.
Source input from which one or more partial intent signals may be extracted.
Tooling metadata for a read-only review selection, not a proposed SpecGraph domain concept.
Tooling metadata describing a source package selected for a review, not a proposed domain concept.

policies.text: SpecGraph Core v0 is a draft compiler-backed seed and does not authorize canonical SpecGraph mutations or trusted ontology publication.

relations.description: The verifier checks the published bundle against the retained bundle and produces an observation on success.
A code surface implements a specification.
A constraint applies to graph nodes.
SpecGraph contains graph edges.
SpecGraph contains graph nodes.
SpecGraph contains specification artifacts.
A decision constrains a specification.
A spec defines requirements.
An edge relates one or more nodes.
Evidence supports an acceptance criterion.
An intent fragment contributes partial observable meaning to a draft.
A spec has acceptance criteria.
A hypothesis may support, challenge, or contextualize interpretation of a draft.
A hypothesis may support, challenge, or contextualize a proposal without becoming the proposal.
An intent draft motivates a candidate proposal without being replaced by it.
A draft records originating observed meaning for a governed product intent; the relationship does not itself grant approval.
A governed product intent motivates a candidate proposal without being replaced by it.
An invariant governs valid SpecGraph evolution.
A node is connected by an edge.
A spec refines product intent.
A release packages code surfaces.
A requirement is validated by acceptance criteria.
A test validates a requirement.
The draft has a proposed canonical destination; no publication is implied.
An actor attempts to materialize the selected draft at the target named by the action.
An actor attempts to promote a proposal to the draft named by the action.
The proposal is a source of the draft; this relation is not itself a promotion record.
A synthesizer interprets a fragment while developing the draft identified by the action.
An author interprets an intent while developing the candidate identified by the action.
A raw input supplies source material for an extracted fragment.
Review metadata describing package selection; it does not connect or approve the selected models.
